name: Orba Lychee-Ginger
description: A sweetly floral lychee soda with a sharp ginger bite, sold in distinctive silver-and-white cans with a holographic label that shifts between pink and gold at different angles. Orba is Vexa's upmarket line, designed to compete in the Tier 2-3 space without the premium pricing of true Tier 3 brands.
flavor_profile: Intensely sweet lychee floral notes, clean and perfume-adjacent, cut by a genuine ginger sharpness that prevents it from being cloying; crisp carbonation
cultural_context: Orba's holographic label is a deliberate aspirational signal — it looks expensive at a glance, which matters in Tier 2 social contexts where appearance of upward mobility is socially significant. Teens and young adults in Tier 2 residential blocks favor it precisely because it photographs well in mesh-net posts. Older Tier 2 residents find this transparently manipulative, which is accurate.
story_hooks: The holographic label technology used by Orba is actually a stripped-down version of military-grade optical camouflage coating — someone in Vexa's procurement chain has been sourcing it illegally, and the defense corponation wants it back.
A mesh-net influencer with a massive Tier 2 following has been secretly paid by Orba for three years — and a leaked contract is about to surface.
A batch of Orba cans from a specific production run has labels that, when photographed under UV light, display a repeating string of coordinates — no one at Orba admits to knowing why.
